consolidate-merge.note: 2026-08-04: extended from merge-only to the full SKEIN v2 repair vocabulary (merge / edge / rename / split). 2026-08-05: RegistryConsolidator is retired from the main pipeline by the synchronous StreamingRepairer (Ψ_repair, repair-judge.md) — this prompt is kept only for the RQ3 order-robustness batch-reference harness.

ladder.note: 2026-08-17: replaced corpus-specific worked examples with a domain-neutral contract derived only from category definitions and observed surfaces. Same-day fix: the first neutral fold test ('<finer> is recorded') carried no attribution, so preserving vs part-of was undecidable from the rewrite; replaced with an attribution-rewrite test over a placeholder event ('<finer> was involved in an event') plus the collection-vs-thing tiebreak — neutral, but the subject can still visibly widen.

listwise-select-complete-v2.note: 2026-08-18 prompt-optimization arm: baseline named choices with explicit completeness, abbreviation guidance, and identifier/version guards.

listwise-select-balanced-v3.note: 2026-08-18 prompt-optimization arm: balanced positive abbreviation and negative version examples while preserving named complete choices.

repair-judge.note: 2026-08-17 amendment: the op-schema line documented `distinct{pair:[A,B]}`, whose A/B metavariables collide with the A./B./C. labels the component listing uses for readability. Measured on the Country probe (run 2026-08-17-country-probe-f7231e6e58e9): gemma4:e2b-16k answered `"pair": ["A","C"]` and ALL 17 repair calls were rejected as `unlisted-entity`, so repair could correct nothing on that model. The slot is now spelled `["<canonical name>","<canonical name>"]` with an explicit never-use-the-letter rule. StreamingRepairer additionally accepts a bare label as a fallback (name match takes precedence). This rotates every runId that includes this prompt.

repair-judge-compact-v1.note: 2026-08-18 prompt-optimization arm: compact schema, complete pair coverage, forbidden signal-as-op labels, and high-confidence explicit-identity merges only.

listwise-select-nameform-v4.note: 2026-08-19 judge-size study: baseline text plus explicit written-form identity rules (vendor prefix, punctuation, bracketed descriptor, extension/platform suffix, generic type word, acronym, transliteration/translation) and the matching non-identity rules (version/edition, part-of, artifact-vs-program, different base name).

listwise-select-nameform-v5.note: 2026-08-19: v4 plus identifier precedence — a structured identifier paired with a descriptive label carries the identity, the bare label is a broader entity. Fixes HackerGroup, regresses Software (x86/x64 confusion).

listwise-select-nameform-v6.note: 2026-08-19: v5 plus exact-identifier matching when options differ only by a code, number, or few characters. Best local arm: pairwise F1 1.000 on Software and HackerGroup dev probes and 1.000 on the Country test probe at k=6, with gemma4:12b-16k.

listwise-graph-v1.note: 2026-08-20: identity ballot (nameform-v6 rules) plus the granularity half — parent option number, relation, and gloss — so one call per document decides both the partition and the edges between its clusters.

listwise-graph-v2.note: 2026-08-20: v1 plus the document-scoped parent pool. Parents are chosen by P-number from every entity the source put on the table, because 14 of 24 reachable gold edges had a parent the identity blocker never retrieved at any depth.

listwise-graph-compact-v3.note: 2026-08-20: compact dialect — one E-numbered entity list shared by identity and parents, M-numbered mentions, single-letter keys, and a level code so entities get rungs. Cuts the repeated name/category strings that dominate the verbose dialect output.

listwise-graph-compact-v4.note: 2026-08-20: compact-v3 plus the two rules its errors called for — a written-form variant is identity and never a parent edge (the pool run expressed two gold merges as edges instead), and a substitution test separating narrower-of from part-of (it labelled components as coarsenings).

listwise-graph-compact-v5.note: 2026-08-20: v4 with the identifier-precedence rule restored in full. Compressing it to one clause cost HackerGroup identity 1.000 -> 0.500 — the judge linked APT28 (UAC-0028) to the bare label APT28 instead of to UAC-0028, which is the half of the rule the compression dropped.

listwise-graph-compact-v6.note: 2026-08-20: v4 with the identifier-precedence rule restored to its VERBATIM nameform-v6 wording. v5 tried a stronger phrasing (never the bare label; it belongs in the parent slot) which fixed HackerGroup and destroyed Software — 4 links instead of 15, identity 0.000.

listwise-graph-compact-v7.note: 2026-08-20: the lean correct variant — compact-v3 structure with ONLY the identifier-precedence rule restored to its verbatim nameform-v6 wording. v4 added an anti-collapse clause and a substitution test on top; this drops both, to test whether they earn their place or merely load the prompt.

ladder-placed-v2.note: 2026-08-21: the ladder prompt plus placements — where each supplied example sits on the ladder it just derived. The call has already read those surfaces, so the catch-up pass that gives pre-ladder entities their rungs costs no extra LLM call.
